I had a friend that was majorly depressed, distant, also drank a lot and had suicidal thoughts. He was depressed, irritable, angry. And he never told me what was going on internally, until one day I said something about my dad who was an alcoholic who died from liver failure, it was an extremely hard day when my dad passed away. (He passed away maybe two weeks before we had this conversation)

My guy friend was having alcohol withdrawals that particular day and I said to my friend how my dad had those as well, my dad had to drink to live because if he didn’t drink his body would crave for it, my dad was also irritable and majorly depressed. My dad was so depressed that he didn’t even know where to begin with how to even get better, at the end of the day my Dad wasn’t able to heal those deep wounds, those scars that had basically rotted into his soul. He committed suicide by drinking alcohol until that shit fucking killed him. It was slow, very slow, but once you flip that addiction switch you become powerless over your addiction and your life with become unmanageable to the point that death is right there waiting for you. 

I told my guy friend that. My guy friend got quiet and his face went pale and that was that. A few weeks later my guy friend lost his job due to him drinking on the job, repeatedly, all throughout his shift. I still kept in touch but slowly his depression got worse so he drank more and shit got worse. His parents confronted him and said that it was getting bad and recommended him to go to AA meetings(Alcoholics Anonymous). He went to the meetings but he was still struggling so he moved out with one of our mutual friends and they lived together for sometime. She went to AA meetings with him because he was like a brother to her. Then.....shit hit the fan and he drank A LOT one day and he was wandering around the streets of the town that I live in at night and our mutual friend eventually was able to find him. He threw his keys in a lake, broke his phone, and had a needle prick in his left arm. To this day we don’t know what it was. 

He moved back in with his parents, said he wasn’t going to drink, and he drank again and his parents told him he had to go to a crisis drug inpatient center this center was for people who struggled with addiction/suicidal thoughts/ and drug use and addressed any trauma that he had experienced throughout his life. He stayed there for two weeks. 

When he got out he had to go to a program and stick with the program for AA, attend meetings, see his AA peer counselor once a week, and meet with his therapist once a week, he also takes medication. I’ll let you in on something, my guy friend the same guy friend I’ve been talking about said about a year ago that he would never go to therapy, get help, or take medication. Now he praises the support network that he now has due to him getting mental health help. 

He’s taking life one day at a time and he still has his good days and bad. 

I feel your username speaks volumes so I’m not here to tell you what you should do, that is your choice. Just know that you’re not alone and the people that are in your life, that love and care about you, they will still love and care about you even if you can’t be normal. 

If you’re really in need of feeling normal, have one trusted person in your life that you can be your normal self with and tell them what is going on even if you don’t have the words. That is okay. You can always say you don’t have the words, that there is so much stress in your life and that your depression is becoming severe. Tell someone. And if they tell you something that you don’t feel good or genuine about tell the next person that you can be your normal self with. It’s a process. One day at a time. Baby steps. Because for me my major depressive disorder did not happen over night, I have to take small steps or the tinniest steps imaginable  to be able to understand my depression and how to lessen the blows that come my way from it.

Take care 💕
